capacity_levers.default: no authoritative default captured this unit; live box shows 64 [live]
capacity_levers.recommended: 320-640 for this shape (5 slots/request under extra_buffer -> 64 slots caps you at ~12 concurrent; 320 slots ~ 64 concurrent)
capacity_levers.works_with_hybrid: yes - mamba/hybrid only; it is a SLOT COUNT, not a token budget
capacity_levers.quote: [snippet] "--mamba-full-memory-ratio 4.59 ... --max-mamba-cache-size 320 state/slot 153.9 MB ... the ratio prices 5 state slots per request; ... so 64 concurrent requests pin 320 slots"
capacity_levers.expected_effect: Raises the number of resident recurrent-state slots. This is the most plausible clamp on our 15.9-16.5% resident window: 1,620,892 declared tokens with only ~16% resident is a CONCURRENCY/SLOT ceiling (64 slots / 5 per req = ~12 requests), not a KV-token shortage.

capacity_levers.default: DISPUTED - two secondary sources disagree: 0.9 vs 0.3 (see contradictions)
capacity_levers.recommended: unresolved; do not set blind. It re-splits one fixed memory budget between mamba pool and KV pool
capacity_levers.works_with_hybrid: yes - hybrid only (it is the split knob between state pool and KV pool)
capacity_levers.quote: [snippet of that page] "In SGLang, hybrid linear models separate the memory pool into two parts: Mamba pool and KV cache pool. Both Mamba pool and KV cache pool memory sizes are fixed, hence the risk of CUDA out-of-memory errors is eliminated. Users can adjust the size ratio between Mamba pool and KV cache pool by changing server argument -mamba-full-memory-ratio" (fetch of the page returned title only - quote is from the search snippet, not the fetched body)
capacity_levers.expected_effect: Trades KV tokens for state slots inside the SAME --mem-fraction-static budget. On our box mem-fraction-static 0.45 already sits at the crash-loop boundary, so raising this without raising the budget can only move capacity, not create it.

capacity_levers.default: off [live: enable_hierarchical_cache=false]; --hicache-ratio default not captured this unit
capacity_levers.recommended: only after the slot/concurrency clamp above is ruled out. If used: --hicache-ratio 2 (host tier = 2x device pool)
capacity_levers.works_with_hybrid: PARTIALLY - HiCache tiers KV pages (L1 HBM / L2 host DRAM / L3 storage). No source found saying mamba/recurrent state is offloaded by HiCache; assume state stays on-device.
capacity_levers.quote: [snippet] "--enable-hierarchical-cache: Enables hierarchical KV cache/offload --hicache-ratio: The ratio of the size of host KV cache memory pool to the size of device pool. Lower this number if your machine has less CPU memory. --hicache-write-policy: Write policy (e.g., write_through for synchronous host writes)"
capacity_levers.expected_effect: Adds host-DRAM KV capacity, so it can raise resident KV tokens - but it does NOT raise mamba slots, and on a unified-memory GB10 box the host pool competes with the same physical memory.

session_cache.what_it_protects: [secondhand, R-SGL.md:39] keeps a session's nodes alive past the request as SOFT protection (not a pin); eviction order is unreferenced -> fewest session refs -> policy score.
session_cache.single_agent_long_session: [secondhand] only implemented by UnifiedRadixCache; a wrong or forgotten session_id silently degrades to plain LRU. Published figure attributed to it (same blog as unified tree): 2.9%-16.6% lower TTFT vs HiRadixCache+LRU on SWE-bench. For ONE agent holding ONE long session this is the closest documented fit, but it protects the session's prefix - it does not create mamba slots, so it cannot lift the ~16% resident ceiling by itself.

top3.why: 64 slots x 5 slots/request (extra_buffer) ~ 12 concurrent requests; with --max-running-requests 5 the resident window is slot-bound, which is the most consistent explanation of 15.9-16.5% of 1,620,892 declared tokens. Try 320-640.

best_capacity_lever: --max-mamba-cache-size: it is the only lever that plausibly explains and lifts the 15.9-16.5% resident ceiling on a hybrid model, because the ceiling is a slot/concurrency arithmetic, not a KV-token shortage (1,620,892 declared tokens, ~16% resident).
